body: In PowerPoint on Windows, which key starts the slide show from the first slide?
explanation: F5 starts from the beginning. Shift + F5 starts from the current slide.

body: Which shortcut adds a new slide?
explanation: Ctrl + M inserts a new slide. Ctrl + N opens a new presentation and Ctrl + D duplicates the selected item.

body: What is the effect shown when moving from one slide to the next called?
explanation: Transitions apply between slides; animations apply to objects on a slide.

body: Where do you type notes that only the presenter should see?
options: The Notes pane below the slide
A text box at the slide edge
explanation: Speaker notes are hidden from the audience and appear in Presenter View.

body: What is the default file extension for a PowerPoint presentation?
explanation: .pptx is the current PowerPoint format. .docx is Word and .xlsx is Excel.

body: Which view shows small thumbnails of all slides so you can quickly reorder them?
explanation: Slide Sorter shows every slide as a thumbnail; drag them to change the order.

body: What is good practice for text on a slide?
options: Full paragraphs copied from your report
A few short bullet points per slide
Several different fonts on each slide
Very small text so more fits
explanation: Slides support what you say. Short points are easier for the audience to read while listening.

body: Which key ends a running slide show?
explanation: Esc exits the slide show. Enter and Space move to the next slide.

body: Which tab has commands to insert pictures, tables and charts?
explanation: The Insert tab holds pictures, shapes, tables, charts, SmartArt and media.

body: What is a ready-made set of colours, fonts and effects applied to the whole presentation called?
explanation: Themes (Design tab) keep the look consistent across all slides.

body: What does Shift + F5 do?
options: Starts the slide show from the first slide
Starts the slide show from the current slide
explanation: Shift + F5 is handy when rehearsing a specific part of the deck.

body: You want the college logo in the same corner of every slide. What is the best way?
options: Add it once in the Slide Master
Paste it onto each slide by hand
Put it in the speaker notes
Add it to the first slide only
explanation: Objects on the Slide Master appear on every slide that uses its layouts, and you change them in one place.

body: What does Presenter View show the presenter?
options: The current slide, the next slide, speaker notes and a timer
explanation: Presenter View appears on your screen while the audience sees only the slide.

body: What is the Format Painter used for?
options: Setting a picture as the slide background
Copying formatting from one object or text to another
explanation: Select the formatted item, click Format Painter, then click the target to apply the same formatting.

body: You want bullet points to appear one at a time as you click. What should you do?
options: Apply an entrance animation to the text box, with effect options set to By Paragraph
explanation: Entrance animations set to By Paragraph reveal one bullet per click.

body: Which feature turns a bulleted list into a diagram such as a process, cycle or hierarchy?
explanation: Use Convert to SmartArt (Home tab) or Insert > SmartArt.

body: Why add Alt Text to images in a presentation?
options: To lock the image in place
So screen readers can describe the image to people who cannot see it
explanation: Alt Text makes slides accessible when they are shared as a file.

body: You have a backup slide you only want to show if someone asks during Q&A. What is the best option?
options: Delete it and recreate it later
Move it to a separate file
Hide the slide, then jump to it only if needed
Make its text white so it is invisible
explanation: Hidden slides are skipped in the show but stay in the file, and you can still jump to them.

body: Which tool records how long you spend on each slide while practising?
explanation: Rehearse Timings (Slide Show tab) times each slide so you can check you fit the time limit.

body: Your deck is 80 MB because of large photos and is too big to email. What should you do first?
options: Use Compress Pictures to reduce the image resolution
Split the text into more slides
explanation: Photos are usually the bulk of the file size. Compressing them shrinks the file with little visible change on screen.

body: Which colour combination is hardest for the audience to read on a projector?
options: Black text on a white background
White text on a dark blue background
Dark grey text on a light cream background
Light yellow text on a white background
explanation: Readable slides need strong contrast between text and background. Projectors also wash out pale colours.

body: Three boxes on a slide are unevenly spaced. Which command spaces them equally?
explanation: Select the shapes, then use Distribute to make the gaps between them equal.

body: What does the Morph transition do?
options: Converts the slides into a video
Smoothly animates objects that appear on both of two consecutive slides from their old to their new position, size or colour
explanation: Duplicate a slide, move or resize objects on the copy, and Morph animates the change.

body: You changed the font in the Slide Master, but one slide still shows the old font. What is the most likely reason?
options: Text on that slide has direct formatting that overrides the master
The master only affects new presentations
Fonts cannot be changed in the master
explanation: Formatting applied directly to text wins over the master. Reset the slide (Home > Reset) or clear the formatting.

body: You want to share your deck so it looks the same on any device and is not easily edited. What is the best format?
options: Paste the text into an email
explanation: A PDF keeps the layout and fonts fixed and opens on almost every device.

body: A custom font looks right on your laptop but is replaced on the venue's computer. What prevents this?
options: Embed the fonts when saving (File > Options > Save)
explanation: Embedding stores the font inside the file so another computer can display it.

body: An animation should start on its own 2 seconds after the previous one finishes. Which settings do this?
explanation: After Previous waits for the prior effect to end; Delay adds the extra wait.

body: Which structure works best for a 5-minute project presentation?
options: Problem, what you built, result or demo, what you learned, next steps
Only a title slide and a thank-you slide
Thirty slides showing all of the code
explanation: A clear story helps the panel follow your work and remember the outcome.

body: What is the Selection Pane used for?
options: Naming, hiding and reordering overlapping objects on a slide
explanation: Selection Pane (Home > Arrange) lists every object, which helps when shapes are stacked or hard to click.

body: The projector is widescreen, but your slides show black bars on both sides. What is the most likely cause?
options: The slide size is set to 4:3 instead of 16:9
explanation: A 4:3 slide on a 16:9 screen is letterboxed. Change it under Design > Slide Size.
